body: @cwilso any possibility of getting a chance to socialize the pros/cons in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10378 on today's call and get early feedback?

Yup, we did cover that in the meeting, even though I failed to see this request ahead of the meeting (sorry). Minutes from the meeting: - Chairing and Notes: Johnny Stenback is currently stepping in as the chair for the meetings, replacing Chris, who is no longer with Google. Johnny Stenback confirmed that Gemini is taking notes for the meeting, which will assist in posting summaries afterward. - Carryover: Stage Three Request for Patching Issue (Issue 11542): The group confirmed that the stage three request for patching issue 11542 remains blocked because Mozilla is waiting for Henry Sivonen to review it. Olli Pettay and Johnny Stenback agreed that this issue is currently blocking other work, and it will be carried over in the notes until the necessary review is complete. - Carryover: Coherent Story for HTML Setting Methods (Issue 11669): This item can be removed from the carryover agenda because it is no longer blocked. Noam Rosenthal reported that they took over upstreaming the sanitizer, and a large pull request is currently under review, resolving the blocking issue. - Declarative Keyboard Focus Navigation (Issue 11649): Jacques Newman is requesting movement to Stage 3 for declarative keyboard focus navigation for scope set of composite widgets because they are hoping to ship it soon. Jacques Newman is asking for reviews to get feedback before shipping and committed to spending time addressing the popover behavior discussed with Luke, including potentially updating the specification to opt these elements out by default. - Spellcheck Custom Dictionary/Exemptions (Issue 12388): Brian Kardell introduced issue 12388, which proposes a way to list exemptions so that certain terms (like domain terms or proper nouns) are not flagged as spelling errors by the spellcheck. Olli Pettay expressed uncertainty about whether the proposal would work with all languages, such as Finnish, and needs to discuss it internally with Emily. The group agreed to keep this item on the agenda for the next meeting to allow Mozilla time for internal discussion. - Form Control Range Interface (Issue 11478): Stephanie Zhang provided an update on the opaque range (form control range interface, issue 11478), which they plan to ship soon in Chromium and which allows developers to create ranges over controls' value text. Stephanie Zhang is requesting feedback on the current specification pull requests, giving a heads-up that they plan to propose Stage 3 in a future meeting. - Customizable Select UI Behavior (Issue 12328): The group discussed concerns about allowing interactive content inside options in a customizable select (issue 12328). Joey Arhar, Luke, and Mason Freed agreed that the status quo should remain, where interactive content is not arbitrarily outlawed in options, as doing so might push authors to use non-native elements, making it harder for the browser to provide warnings and accessibility support. Dan Clark noted that the Chromium implementation coerces the ARIA role of the pop-up to a dialogue if interactive content is present, helping accessibility, which may be a useful fallback. - Overscroll Areas via Command Equals Toggle (Issue 12273): This topic concerns a feature that allows adding elements into overscroll areas of other elements (issue 12273), and the task force has already promoted it to Stage 1. The group confirmed that Stage 1 can be cleared in a task force setting, but Stage 2 onward should still be addressed in this meeting, and they will seek Stage 2 approval shortly. Johnny Stenback noted that the process should track stage changes to ensure everything reflects reality. - Row Rule Properties Inheritance (Issue 11095): Kurt Catti-Schmidt provided an update that the discussion confirmed that row rule properties should eventually be updated to live in the CSS specification, and the agenda plus label can be taken off for now. A pull request and follow-up issue to move these properties will be filed shortly after Kevin's return from leave. - Reference Target Event Handling (Issue 10707): Dan Clark introduced an issue regarding event handling with the reference target proposal, specifically how to handle uncomposed events that fire in a shadow DOM and need to be observable by the source element in the light DOM. Dan Clark proposed a "redispatching" or retargeting mechanism for trusted events in the source element's tree to ensure the source can listen to the event, similar to related target behavior. After discussion, Dan Clark agreed to continue drafting the specification with the goal of scoping the new behavior to trusted events to avoid potential compatibility issues and to seek feedback from Apple. - Reference Target Stage Advancement (Issue 10707): Dan Clark suggested that the reference target proposal meets the bar for Stage 2, noting that there is a draft specification, a positive standards position from Mozilla, and only rough edges remain, such as the eventing issue. Since there were no objections, the group agreed that the proposal should move to Stage 2, and the chair will add the appropriate label to the issue. - Responsive Video Poster Images (Issue 10378): Scott Jehl from Squarespace presented issue 10378 concerning the video element's poster image, which cannot currently be responsive or exposed in an accessible way. The team explored a plan to use the existing `` or `` elements as children of the video element to control the poster, gaining functionality like `srcset` and an `alt` attribute for accessibility. An alternative approach involves adding new attributes like `poster-srcset` and `poster-sizes` to the video and source elements. - Next Steps for Responsive Video Poster Images (Issue 10378): Scott Jehl plans to create a side-by-side comparison of the two proposals and post it to the issue to gather further feedback. The group noted that this topic is already at the level of Stage 1, requiring an explainer, which could be accomplished by a well-rounded comment or an edit to the original issue post that summarizes the latest proposal.
